name: NeuralPath Horizon Standard Neural Mesh
description:
The NeuralPath Horizon Standard is a full-spectrum consumer neural mesh delivering always-on feed access, augmented reality overlay, encrypted messaging, biometric payment integration, and civic identity verification through a distributed cortical lattice implanted across the prefrontal and temporal lobes. The mesh operates at 4.2 Gbps sustained throughput with 128-bit rolling encryption on all financial and identity transactions, supports up to six simultaneous AR overlay channels, and draws power from a bioelectric harvesting cell rated for fifteen years before capacitor replacement. Firmware updates push automatically during sleep cycles, requiring no user intervention beyond an annual clinic recalibration.

The Horizon Standard is the single most common BCI in GLMZ — estimates suggest it accounts for nearly thirty percent of all active neural interfaces in the city's Tier 2 and Tier 3 population. Factory workers use it to clock in without touching a terminal; parents use it to monitor children's location feeds; transit riders use it to pay fares with a blink. It is so unremarkable that people rarely mention having one, the way previous generations never mentioned having a phone number. The chip carries a faint social stigma in elite circles — calling someone a 'Horizon head' implies they are ordinary, replaceable, a face in the crowd — but in the Shelf and working wards, it is simply what adults have.
installation_requirements: Licensed outpatient clinic; procedure takes approximately 90 minutes under local anesthetic with automated implant array
rejection_risk: Low — NeuralPath's biocompatible polymer lattice has a 97.3% acceptance rate across diverse neural architectures; rare rejection cases present within 72 hours
maintenance: Automatic firmware updates during sleep; annual recalibration at any NeuralPath-certified clinic (Φ45 standard fee); bioelectric cell replacement every 15 years

side_effects: Mild phosphene flicker during firmware updates (approximately 3-7 minutes, typically nocturnal)
Low-grade tinnitus in the first two weeks post-installation as auditory cortex adapts to feed audio channels
Occasional notification bleed — AR overlays briefly visible in peripheral vision during stress or fatigue
Minor short-term memory fragmentation reported in roughly 4% of users during the first month of operation
cultural_context: The Horizon Standard is the democratic floor of neural connectivity in GLMZ — having one signals that you are a functioning member of society, paying taxes, riding transit, and existing in the civic record. Not having one is far more remarkable and often suspicious. In Tier 3 neighborhoods it is considered a responsible adult purchase, often gifted to teenagers at coming-of-age milestones. In Tier 2, many employers subsidize installation as a condition of hire. The chip carries no prestige but also no shame — it is infrastructure, as neutral as pavement.
known_users: elderly residents on assisted care plans
story_hooks: A batch of Horizon Standards distributed through a subsidized Tier 2 clinic has been quietly loaded with a secondary mesh that records conversations and routes them to an unknown recipient — the players must trace the supply chain before the next firmware push locks the backdoor in permanently.

A young woman's Horizon Standard is the only record that she witnessed a corporate homicide — the problem is that NeuralPath's data is legally owned by the company, not the user, and the corporation wants it wiped.

A fixer needs to move through a district where every NeuralPath Horizon mesh is integrated with a municipal surveillance dragnet — they need someone who can spoof a Horizon signal without actually having one installed.
